findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The owner’s CFM certification is expired, this has been a repeat violation in the past.  She has been given information for the CFM classes held at SCDPH and is planning on signing up for the March class.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S) DATED 11/18/2022 AND 6/12/2023.

The person-in-charge (PIC) does not have a valid Certified Food Manager certificate at this time. Inspector discussed the need for certification and discussed the testing process. PIC is aware that should operations continue the certificate must be renewed but she is considering ending operations. Maintain contact with SCDPH regarding permitting and certification requirements.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Kitchen hand sink and the restroom hand sinks need to be re-caulked.  The caulk present is cracked and wearing away, allowing moisture to become trapped between the hand sink and wall.  Ensure sinks are re-caulked to provide an easily cleanable and smooth surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Baffles were observed to contain an accumulation of dust and grease debris.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be kept clean to prevent food contamination.  Ensure baffles are cleaned in between professional cleaning scheduling.

(C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Employee blocked hand sink with bus tub after inspector had advised once to ensure hand sink is not blocked/remains accessible for handwashing. Bus tub removed from handsink. Education provided.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

Chlorine bleach concentration in 3rd sink compartment sink registered at 0ppm on test strips. COS-education provided. Ensure enough bleach is added, per manufacturers instructions to create a concentration of 100ppm for sanitizing step.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-703.11: Observed staff member place bleach in both 2nd and 3rd compartment of the ware washing sink. COS- education provided. Warewashing in a commercial setting is a 3-step process: wash, rinse, and sanitize. Ensure wares are washed with soap in sink 1, rinsed in sink 2, and then submerged in sanitizer solution in sink 3 in accordance with label directions for bleach,

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Gallon of milk observed with no date label. Inspector discussed with PIC labeling requirements for QBC under FDA food code. 
Also stores personal food in some of the fridges, discussed that items for personal/family use should be designated as such and inspector will not look for datemarking on those items.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Thermometers were not present in all refrigerators. Make sure all refrigerators have thermometers in them (which can be hard in a shared kitchen).
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

750-830a All equipment and utensils placed in dish machines shall be exposed to all dishwashing cycles.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Bulk items not immediately easily recognizable were not labeled. Label these items with common name of item.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment:

750-830a Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Dish machines shall be operated in accordance with the manufacturers instructions. Automatic dispensers and liquid injectors, if any, shall be properly installed and maintained.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: (A) There are food splatters on the ceiling above the stove.   (B) An electrical plate is missing where the Kelvinator refrigerator/freezer is plugged (the back hallway).    750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.  Clean the ceiling and replace the electrical plate.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Two sets of fluorescent lights in the back food storage area (near Kelvinator and Hotpoint refrigerators are located) have no covers over the bulbs.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.
Place covers or shields over the bulbs.
